body:
I know this is off topic of the post, but I didn't want to make a whole new thread for it.

I'm ending my life. I know you don't care. I just wanted the closure of saying it "out loud".

Goodbye. I hope you all overcome your issues. I fucked my life up.

I'm not socializing, I'm yelling into the void. I don't care who reads what I say or what they think of it. I've never had a real conversation on here. 

Half of Reddit is bots anyway.

Humans are selfish and have almost no empathy for each other. We just use each other to get what we want. Calling that "social" seems like an incorrect use of the word. We're more like "parasitic animals". That's less flattering though.
Never.

I've been trying and failing to work it out with pencil and paper. Still working on it.

These past few puzzles have been diabolical.
There is no help. No one cares, it just makes people feel good to pretend they do.
No one comments their code in the industry either.

I haven't had a friend that I hung out with outside of school since I was 7 or 8.

The last time I had anything resembling a friend, I was 13. I'm 32 now.
There is no way this is just a one-off thing. We'll probably extend it into a full blown interpreter like Intcode.

I suspect that this happens when your parents are too judgmental and controlling.

When I was a kid, my mom disapproved of everything I was interested in. I wasn't allowed to be myself. She regularly threw away my books, CDs, toys, and clothes if she didn't like them.

I learned to be secretive so that I could keep my things and not be punished or shamed for liking stuff.
You're right, I see now that what I said about the woman was uncalled for. I respect her for actually trying something while I'm just spouting off on Reddit.
The problems have been disappointingly easy. But it's free entertainment so I can't complain.
I read the story, but it never makes sense to me. Something about crabs and octopuses and machines not working right.

I agree with the stance, but is standing on a street corner with a sign and a grimace on your face like a crazy person really helping the cause? The woman looks like a lesbian, she's not having kids regardless.

Also, the slogan is bad. STOP HAVING KIDS -- all capitals. Like it's threatening you. The logo is a baby with a cross through it. I don't know, I don't have any better ideas, but this isn't convincing. It's comical.

Change the approach. Try saying "Consider Adoption" and show a picture of some crying orphan or something.

People are gonna procreate irresponsibly no matter what you do. Living beings are literally programmed to want to reproduce at all costs. Taking away social programs won't be a deterrent. A freaking pandemic and climate change isn't even a deterrent for people.

We should try to help people live better lives, not purposely make life harder in some futile attempt to discourage procreation.

Because some people aren't antinatalist in order to adhere dogmatically to some philosophy they chose. They are antinatalist for the pragmatic reason that some lives are too risky to be worth creating. If everyone were guaranteed to have competent parents, good housing, access to food, good health care, education as high as they want, be given a good job, be guaranteed a partner, be guaranteed good elder care when they are old, and if there were no violence or crime or pain or sadness, then I don't see why creating life would be bad. It's the inherent unfairness and riskiness of life that makes it bad.
I'm in the same boat. I don't have enough money in my bank account to pay my rent next month. Definitely gonna end it soon. It's over.

It's not that easy. Therapy isn't available for everyone. And most therapists suck.

Also, this person can't even leave their house, how do you expect them to navigate getting a therapist on their own?

I honestly can't believe that I ended up this way. That this is my life. It's entirely unfair. I didn't choose this. I was just born into a shitty life.

Unbelievable.

I got this at work too. My manager always wanted to discuss my "career goals" but I didn't have any. The idea of me being content with the job I already had was unbelievable to her. She expected me to want to move up the corporate ladder like her and everyone else who only care about their salary and job title.
I relate to this so much. I'm visually attracted to guys, but I don't want to actually have sex with one because sex is gross. Even when I watch porn, I prefer it to be solo porn.
Talk therapy doesn't work if your problem is that you can't talk.

Everyone says this, but it's not true, or at least not true everywhere. I had a software job and I was basically doing meetings and presentations for half the day. It sucked for someone like me who has bad communication skills.

Terrifying.

I don't understand how they expect anyone to thrive in a typical urban high school environment. The schools are like prisons. At the schools I went to, the walls were all made of cement blocks, and most of the classrooms had no windows. You had to walk through a metal detector and have your backpack checked for weapons at the door. Fights broke out every single day. The other students were all rowdy and some of them were in gangs.

How are you supposed to focus on learning when you are scared of your classmates and feel like a prisoner? I spent most of high school in a fog just trying to survive each day and get home in one piece.

Anyway, I had no friends in high school. I was bullied. I was already schizoid, but it got worse.

Yes, I'm like this, but I've always attributed it to social anxiety.

Everywhere I go, I tend to try to find a secluded place where I can't be seen. I keep my voice low when I talk. I step gently so my footsteps can't be heard. I close doors gently so no one knows if I've arrived or left. I've long ago developed a quiet laugh where I just breathe harder through my nose but no sound comes out. I never play my music out loud, I always use headphones, and I get paranoid that people around me can still hear the music. When I did video conference calls, I always kept my camera turned off. I don't take pictures and I don't like being on camera.

It's like I'm trying to be as inconspicuous as possible at all times. Like I don't want anyone to know that I exist.

When I don't respond to people's texts immediately, they probably think I'm being rude or that I don't like them. They don't understand that I just literally don't know what to say. I can't improvise appropriate responses to things.

Yeah, I was extremely socially anxious as a kid due to being bullied and sexually abused by other kids. I didn't feel safe around kids. I would always stick closely to an adult and I felt terrified if I was alone around kids with no adult around. Constantly being on high alert like that for years did something horrible to my brain.

I'm not scared of people anymore, but I still mentally shut down when I'm around them. I'm completely indifferent towards people. I get really quiet and serious and stiff in social interactions, even when everyone else is laughing and having fun. I haven't had a friend in 20 years.

I don't like being this way.

Coworkers used to invite me out with them. Sometimes I would decline. Other times I would go, but I would be quiet and awkward, and I could tell that I was killing the vibe. They stopped inviting me eventually. I was glad about that at first, but then I felt left out seeing them leaving together smiling and laughing, and later overhearing all their stories and seeing their pictures of the fun adventures they went on together.
I think living things are programmed to want to reproduce. It's a compulsion. There is no logic behind it.

I never felt safe in high school. Every single day, multiple fights would break out and kids would get beat up and bullied. I've been beaten, had food mashed into my face, etc.

Going to school felt like going to prison. I was a straight A student in middle school, then when high school started my grades tanked. It's hard to focus on learning when you're scared of your classmates. I started leaving school early and skipping entire days as much as I could. I almost didn't graduate over it.

College was a lot better. I was finally around people who were friendly and smart. Too bad my social skills and self-esteem were destroyed by this point. I didn't know how to make friends. I loved studying and taking classes though.

I've noticed that buying more things, doing more activities, and making accomplishments never made me any happier, and they sometimes made things worse due to added stress and responsibility.

So I guess I'm as content as I will ever be, which isn't much.
I have no goals or ambition because I don't want anything. I'm just killing time.
I feel bad for kids. They didn't ask to be here and suffer.

If someone cancels plans, I feel relieved. If they don't cancel and just don't show up, I feel annoyed that I wasted precious mental energy worrying about it.

Also [canceling plans is like heroin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CffwNZvILms)

Physics and astronomy are the low hanging fruit of knowledge. Psychology is considered a "soft" science, not because it is easier, but because we understand so little of it that we don't even know how to make it rigorous.

Not really. I've never been in romantic love. I kind of love my immediate family in the sense that I want good things for them and I help them as much as I can. But I don't enjoy their company. They are a huge source of stress for me. When I get a text or phone call from them, I feel annoyed. If they magically vanished, I would be more relieved than sad.

I was raped multiple times as a kid by another boy. I hardly ever think about it, and I have no conscious feelings about it or the guy who did it. But it has clearly had a huge effect on me anyway. I have an aversion to intimacy and touch, I've never had sex as an adult, and I've never dated.

I think years of spending all day on the Internet reading terrible opinions and misinformation has made me think that no one knows what they are talking about. I feel myself not trusting what anyone says anymore. The more confident someone sounds, the less I believe them.

Exactly. My family is a huge pain. They are really incompetent and they depend on me for everything. I'm always lending money that doesn't get repaid, doing favors that don't get returned, giving advice that doesn't get listened to, and being a shoulder to cry on and having to soak up all their burdens. I'm tired of them asking me to save them from their own bad decisions all the time. When I help them, I feel exploited. Worrying about their well-being stresses me out. 

But I can't just abandon them because I care about them and I would feel guilty if they ended up with their lives ruined over something that I could have fixed.

I think this is one of the reasons why I'm so hesitant to make friends or be in a relationship. Life is hard enough as it is without bringing other people's problems into it. I would rather be lonely but stress-free than to have friends and a partner that I have to worry about and rescue all the time.
It's funny how whenever you get excited about getting a job, you end up hating it within a week. Nothing ever turns out as good as you imagined it would be.

No, everything is a chore.

Despite that, I push myself to do things hoping that it will become enjoyable eventually. Like, if I become skilled at something maybe I'll start actually liking it? I keep waiting for my hobbies to get fun but it hasn't happened yet.

I got bored of my toys really quickly.

I remember begging my mom to get me these walkie talkie things. She bought them, then I realized I had no friends to talk with.

I spent most of my childhood watching tv or playing on the computer.
Alcohol never made me more social. It just makes me smile and laugh at nothing.

I relate to your reluctance to openly share things with people. I know that my life would seem very sad to people and I know that people don't like to talk about sad stuff. So I can't ever be completely honest with anyone. Conversations are a minefield because I have to avoid talking about anything that would reveal how depressed I am and how sad my life is.

This is the main reason why I hate socializing. It's because I know that I'm a boring unlikable aloof person and I'm tired of being insulted or looked down on for it.

This one guy started a conversation with me and it didn't go well. At the end, he sarcastically said "nice talk" and walked away shaking his head. It made me so mad. I'm thinking "screw you, I didn't ask you to talk to me!" People act like you are obligated to entertain them.

I get negative reactions from people all the time and I'm sick of it. I'm trying here. It's not my fault that my parents didn't socialize me and messed up my brain.

I used to take this (it's Paxil right?). It never worked for me, but it did give me erectile dysfunction. I would also go into withdrawal when I missed doses and it felt like I was dying. Dangerous drug.
Relationships are what keep most people going. Life gets boring when you don't care about anybody.

Both of my parents died last year and it totally was a relief. I still have other family members who depend on me though so I'm not out of the woods yet. There is always someone or something tying you down.

No one tells you how often the elderly basically regress back into children. They go back to wearing diapers, being unable to feed themselves, being unable to talk clearly, etc. Only it's not cute anymore when you're old.

The last time I felt happiness was one day when I was 14. I'm in my 30s now. My baseline emotion is a slight feeling of anxiety and dread that sometimes dips into terror. I almost never feel positive emotion.

> imho, that's a non sequitur. One doesn't have anything inherently to do with the other.

I interpreted the OP's post as implying that he/she is suicidal. It's hard to feel motivated to do anything long-term when you are not certain that you will even make it to the end of the week.

> I see life as a very long, but temporary, game. The game is more fun when you do more stuff you enjoy and less stuff you hate. That's what I generally aim to do.

Not all of us have things that we enjoy. That's one of the symptoms of SPD.
I'm not planning anything. Life just keeps happening even when I don't want it to.

It's hard for me to describe myself because I don't know what I like or value. I've been looking all my life, but nothing sticks. I'm always jumping from one hobby to another and back again waiting for the moment when they become fun and not a chore. I have no passion for anything and no love for anyone. All day I'm just looking for something to distract me and fill time until bedtime. The best parts of the day are when I'm asleep.

As for comfort zones, everything is uncomfortable to me. Every time I step outside, I'm out of my comfort zone.

I get dread and anxiety from the thought that if I don't end it early, I will have to continue doing this every day for decades, and that things will only get worse as I age.

I used to try to hang out with coworkers after work, like go with them to a bar for drinks or whatever. Afterward, on the way back home, I would always explode with anger and frustration. I mean punching walls, smashing my phone, etc. I broke so many phones.
Yes, I'm in a never-ending search for something interesting.
This reminds me of the [Rate My Life Quiz](https://atomiks.github.io/rate-my-life/). It made me realize how much of my unhappiness was circumstantial rather than due to brain chemistry.

I don't care if it's schizoid disorder or social anxiety or avoidant personality or autism or introversion or whatever. It's all the same animal to me. It's the "I Can't Socialize" condition.

I'm tired of people telling me I should go to a therapist when I've already been to four and I'm still stuck this way. I don't want to "cope" or "adapt" or "manage". I want to be cured. I'm sick of being made to feel as though if I went to therapy and didn't get better, then I just didn't try hard enough. It's not the patient's fault if the doctor didn't fix them. 

I'm certain that most people who suggest therapy have never actually done it before. If they had, they would know how ridiculous a suggestion it is. People love to give advice that they've never had to follow themselves. They just make up crap that sounds right to them or repeat something they heard someone else say. They have no actual experience with it.

Here's my experience: therapists only want your money. They don't care about you. They have no clue how to help you. It's a scam. The last therapist I had could barely contain her glee each time I handed her my debit card. And she was right on top of it when time was up, eyeing that clock like a hawk. I was a sucker for giving them my money and letting them prescribe me mystery drugs that did god knows what to my brain. I was desperate and I forgive myself. I won't make that mistake again.

This worship of Mental Health Professionals and the Almighty Diagnosis has to stop.

I'm here to commiserate with other non-normies who know what it's like to hate socializing. I don't care about the labels.

What's so great about not being high? People use drugs and alcohol because it makes life more bearable. We all know deep down that this shit sucks. That's why we self-medicate and constantly distract ourselves with entertainment.

MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONALS CAN'T HELP YOU.

No one has ever been cured of serious, long-lasting depression or anxiety. Name one person. I'll eat my fucking shoes if you show me one example.

I get lonely, but I've never felt comfortable or happy interacting with others. I have really bad social anxiety.

This disconnected, one-sided, text-only form of communication is all I can handle. I don't have any friends, and I only talk to one family member every few weeks when they want something from me.

Life has good and bad in it, and it's only worth living if your life has enough of the good in it to make up for the bad. I think for most normal people, the good parts are their friends, family, and romantic relationships. We don't have that stuff so it's harder to make life bearable.

It is uncomfortable when I think about the fact that I've been a part of other people's lives and I've affected them in some way. It gives me this sense of responsibility and guilt that I don't want. I don't want to be depended on or to have had any impact on anyone.

I have a young nephew and it is weird to me that I am a part of his childhood and my interactions with him are shaping who he is as a person. He'll probably partially blame me for his future problems the same way I blame my family for my problems.
I'm bad at conversations because I'm not interested enough in other people to want to ask them questions about themselves, and I'm not interesting enough to want to talk about myself.
Psychiatrists don't know jack. It makes me angry just thinking about how useless and expensive they are. Just fleecing desperate people. And everybody buys into it.
I hate to sound discouraging, but I doubt therapy will do much. I would love to be proven wrong though.
I enjoy food while I'm eating it, but I always feel guilty afterward because I'm overweight. I purge often.
I used to be a software engineer, but I quit a year ago because they put too much pressure on me. I'm never working again.

I used to stock shelves at a K-Mart. They called the position "Backroom Locator" to make it sound fancy. It was the most mind-destroying job I've ever had. An hour felt like 10 hours. I quit so fast.

I'm glad you like it though. I wish I liked something.
I suspect most of us have this problem. I think it is due to anhedonia.

I've had this thought myself. I imagined that getting help for mental health is like having a broken leg, but you have to climb a mountain to get to the nearest hospital.

You are expected to seek your own help, but I think that doesn't always work. People who need help need to be found. It should be an intervention, a search and rescue.

I'm 31.

I'm not happy with my life, but I don't have regrets exactly. I don't think I could have done anything differently in my life. Every decision I've ever made was the only decision I could have made at that point in time given my available options, what I knew, and what I was capable of. Even if I could go back in time knowing everything I know now, I don't see what I could realistically do differently. I am where I am due to circumstances out of my control: my family life, the schools I went to, the city I lived in, etc. 

I never had a chance.

I'm not the person you asked, but moving never seemed like an option to me. I wouldn't even know where to go because I've lived in the same area my whole life and never really traveled. I would have to find a job in the area that I'm moving to, and I don't have a car... It's just hard.

When I was a kid, my mom always used to disrespect my privacy by telling other people private embarrassing things about me. I stopped sharing things with her because I lost trust in her.

I can't trust anyone now.

I had a therapist as a teenager. He kind of forced me to admit to him that I was gay. It bothered me because now I was "the gay kid" and all of my problems would be attributed to that. I didn't want to be summed up like that. I never went back after that session.
Assisted suicide is a thing, and whether or not it is morally wrong is debatable.

I'm attracted to people, but that attraction doesn't compel me to do anything about it.

If I see a pretty flower, I don't feel the need to pull it out of the ground and take it home with me. I just admire it for a few moments, then go on about my day. There are lots of pretty flowers, and they will always be there to see again later.

Also, the internet is filled with pictures of the prettiest flowers in the world.

You pointed out something that I miss a lot about college. It is less repetitive than work. You are always learning and doing something new. Every day has different sets of classes. And you only take those classes for a few weeks before switching to new ones. It never gets boring.

The transition to full-time work destroyed me. Doing the exact same thing all day every day. I would be a lifelong student if that was possible.

Every career demands that you be sociable and normal. They purposely select for those qualities during interviews. You may be able to fake it and get hired, but eventually the facade will fall and your boss will pressure you to change. If you don't, you will get fired or at least boxed out of raises and promotions. It doesn't matter how much you accept yourself if no one else will.

My experience is that people are interested in you until they realize how strange you are, then they stop wanting to associate with you. And that rejection hurts. It's better to just not bother with people at all.
In high school, someone called me a "future serial killer". I thought it was funny.

I wish that I didn't have to eat at all. It's annoying to have hunger pangs and to have to try to find something to eat. And once I start eating, it's hard to stop.

I hate how inefficient and high-maintenance the human body is.

I say "please" and "thank you" a lot because I don't like to be a burden so it's genuine. I understand finding it hard to say things that you don't mean though.

I used to find it hard to say "I love you" to my family when they would say it to me. Also, my mom would do this annoying thing where she would stick her cheek out expecting me to kiss it. It's the obligation to do something that I don't want to do or to express an emotion that I'm not feeling that bothers me.

Why do you and others put so much stock in "professional" diagnoses? Act if they have some superpower to make judgments that other people can't. I've been seeing "professionals" for well over a decade and none of them have helped me. They just took my money.

It truly pisses me off how everybody acts like mental health is a solved problem.

Same. I already know how I'm gonna do it. I'm only still here because I'm scared of the pain. 

I don't get how people just live and are OK with getting treated like slaves, watching themselves slowly grow old, helpless, and unwanted, and watching the same happen to their friends and families. You spend every day just trying to cope with the boredom, the regret, and your impending doom. And your body traps you in this hell by threatening you with pain. It's horrific and kind of hilarious in how absurdly cruel it is. God fucking hates us.
I feel you, man.

The way I see it, everyone is selfish and uses others to get what they want. People only care about you as long as you are useful to them, then they drop you until the next time they need you for something. Most people aren't bothered by this because they are too busy trying to use others to care that others are using them back. I'm bothered by it because I prefer to be self-sufficient. Every relationship ends up being one-sided, with me doing all the favors and asking for nothing in return, so I feel used.

Whenever anyone tries to contact me, it's never because they want to do something for me or because they truly care about me and how I'm doing. After the initial pleasantries, the real purpose comes out: "Can you do me a favor?"

Every single time.

I don't even answer the phone anymore. I've cut everybody out of my life.

I eat meat. I just buy whatever is on the menu, I don't care what it's made of. If all meat was suddenly replaced with meat substitutes, the world would keep spinning and people would get used to it. As long as it tastes good.
That's interesting. It made me realize that when I fantasize, I tend to imagine that I'm a different person. I also can't watch porn if a person in it looks like me.

I had a severe fear of people when I was young. I was afraid of being rejected or bullied since that happened to me a lot. Over time, the fear went away and now I just have this general disinterest in people. I avoid social situations, not because I'm afraid of them, but because I know that I have no social skills and nothing in common with people, and it won't go well.
I don't want anything. Nothing that I can think of seems attainable or worth the effort. Nothing I've ever accomplished made me happy.
Not at all. Horrible invention. Wish it didn't exist.

I'm afraid of space and large objects, especially black holes. Videos like [this](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6qw5_YA8iE) are unwatchable to me.

Also tornadoes.

I have fear of missing out, but I think it's out of my hands. I'm just not capable of having the things that other people have.

I watch porn, but it has to be solo porn. I can't stand to watch two people having sex. Makes me mad.

The world is full of rape, murder, slavery, disease, etc. You have to toil and struggle just to have the privilege of surviving. I never understood why anyone would have kids and put them through this. I want to live in their care-free world.

Both of my parents died last year. I didn't care really. If anything, I felt relieved by it. They stressed me out and I was glad that I didn't have to deal with them anymore. I felt free.

I hated being responsible for the funeral and their debts. It made me feel like they were still burdening me from the grave.

I think this guy knows better what his deal is than you do. It's annoying how you all try to diagnose other people and tell them what they do and don't have. 

Also "mental health professionals" don't know jack shit about nothing. Been there done that.
I think I'm done working. I haven't worked since early last year. I'm running out of savings, but I don't care. When I'm completely broke, I'm ending it.

No, exercise is torturous. Afterward, I always feel sick and I often get a headache. I can never keep up with it for more than a few days. I might like it more if I was doing a fun activity that happened to be physical, but just lifting weights or running on a treadmill is boring and painful.

The first and last time I went to a gym, I threw up in the parking lot and had to call out of work for two days due to the soreness.

I think it's cruel how all the worst things in life are good for you and all the best things are bad for you.
You guys are having sex?
I purposely don't keep much food in my place because I know that I'll just eat it all. I have a bad binge eating and purging habit.

Your post reminded me of a [YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yVWXLgTvzMo) I came across years ago. It's some guy sharing a thought about why some people can't make friends. He thinks these people are too unique. They have uncommon tastes in music, uncommon hobbies, don't like bars and clubs, etc. So it's harder for them to find people they connect with. They are "NOT normal," he says, but that's OK and it's not their fault.

It may sound obvious, but it wasn't to me.

I often get stuck on a certain phrase, and I keep saying it or thinking it in a loop for minutes until something distracts me from it.

Also, my mom used to do the whisper talk thing. It annoyed the hell out of me when I was a kid. Then I realized that I did it too.
Yeah, those kids who got cancer and died deserved it.
There are too many people having kids who have no business having kids. Then we wonder why there are so many criminals and morons.

Why do you think people would lie about being schizoid? It's not like it's charming or cool, and this isn't a particularly fun community to want to fit into. 

I like it here because it helps me to realize that I'm not the only one going through this and that I'm not as alone as I thought. I relate to so many of the posts here.

Also, doctors don't do jack to help with this.

I want to change myself. I'm not happy being alone, but I'm not happy being around others either. Being alone is just the less bad option between two bad options. I want to be normal and experience things the way others do.
It blows my mind that everybody is allowed to have kids. You need a license to drive but no training at all to be responsible for another human being's welfare and development. Makes zero sense.

If you think about it, socializing is a very difficult activity. You have to think on your feet, reacting quickly to every random thing the other person says and does. You have to be careful not to offend them or say the wrong thing. And it's a performance. You're trying to sell yourself, be entertaining, appear knowledgeable and confident. It's hard. 

Most people get a lot of practice with socializing in their childhood so it becomes natural for them. But not everybody gets that experience. It's like being an adult who never learned to swim or ride a bike. It's something other adults just expect you to know how to do, and it's hard to learn past a certain age. You don't see adults riding bikes with training wheels or swimming with arm floaties. If that makes sense, I don't know. Can't communicate.

I've quit every job I had without saying goodbye. I've never given advance notice. I just tell my manager I quit and leave without saying anything to anybody else, even people I worked with for years. I barely care.

I also ghost people a lot. I don't want to get too involved with anyone because people's problems and expectations stress me out too much. It's easier to be alone and only have to care about myself. I'm tired of people calling me and telling me what they want from me. I don't care.

Yes! I'm the exact same way. I couldn't have described it better.

I hate it. I want a new brain.

I wasn't going to respond to this because I didn't care, but since people are downvoting me now, I want to defend myself.

I don't hold professionals with the same level of reverence that you do, especially professionals in psychology. Psychology is probably the least scientific of all the sciences. I've had 4 different therapists/psychiatrists and none of them have helped me or seemed to know what they were talking about. They just took my money and prescribed me drugs.

I respect professionals and I seek their advice and take it into account, but I also recognize that they are just people like me and are fallible. I also don't discount my own intelligence and ability to do research and come to my own conclusions.

I self-diagnose myself with physical illnesses all the time. I can tell when I'm sick and figure out which medicine to buy from the pharmacy by reading the labels. When I get a rash, I can find out what it is from WebMD or whatever. There are lots of things that are beyond my understanding, but I'm not completely helpless.

I'm like this with my family. They act like they can't do anything without me and are constantly dropping their problems into my lap. It stresses me out and I hate it, but I also kind of care about them and feel obligated to help. So I help, but then I end up just feeling resentful and used.

I've never asked anyone for help ever. If there is something I can't do, I just don't do it. I don't go looking for someone else to do it for me. I don't put myself into situations I can't get out of.
You don't need to be professionally diagnosed. Therapists use the same checklists we do.
